data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Decentralized networks are more resilient when they exhibit genuinely uncorrelated failure modes across diverse operational environments, but the critical evidence to distinguish true independence from hidden shared causes is whether the system's failure correlation structure remains stable under perturbation: if perturbing the operational environment (changing cloud providers, software stacks, geographic regions) changes the correlation structure, then the apparent independence was an artifact of a shared stable environment, not true independence.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the environmental perturbation is so extreme that it overwhelms all systems regardless of their independence, then the test is inconclusive.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the decentralized network cannot practically achieve environmental diversity (e.g., due to cost constraints), then the theoretical resilience is not practically achievable.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the large service also operates across diverse environments (e.g., multi-region, multi-cloud), then the perturbation test does not discriminate between the two architectures.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"True independence of failures means that the probability of failure in one node is unaffected by the state of other nodes. However, in practice, nodes in a decentralized network may appear independent only because they share a common stable environment. When that environment changes (e.g., a common cloud provider experiences an outage, a shared library has a vulnerability), the failures become correlated. The evidence to distinguish true independence from hidden shared causes is to test the stability of the correlation structure under environmental perturbation: if perturbing the environment changes the correlation structure, the independence was merely apparent; if it remains stable, the independence is more likely genuine.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
